notes: EBIT proxy: ‘ebit’ uses AbbVie’s ‘Operating earnings’ line from the consolidated statements of earnings (includes acquired IPR&D/milestones and any impairment charges), not a separately defined EBIT metric. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1551152/000155115226000008/abbv-20251231.htm))

D&A definition: ‘da’ equals Depreciation + Amortization of intangible assets from the cash flow statement reconciling net earnings to cash from operating activities. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1551152/000155115226000008/abbv-20251231.htm))

Capex definition: ‘capex’ equals ‘Acquisitions of property and equipment’ from the cash flow statement (cash outflow line). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1551152/000155115226000008/abbv-20251231.htm))

NWC calculation: NWC = (Total current assets − Cash and equivalents) − (Total current liabilities − Current portion of long-term debt and finance lease obligations). This yields negative NWC consistent with a payables-heavy working-capital model for a pharma distributor/marketer. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1551152/000155115226000008/abbv-20251231.htm))
Current price timing: finance quote timestamp is March 20, 2026; set as_of_date to 2026-03-20.

catalysts: Sustained outperformance/underperformance in Immunology franchise growth (Skyrizi/Rinvoq) and any changes in Humira decline trajectory. ([news.abbvie.com](https://news.abbvie.com/2026-02-04-AbbVie-Reports-Full-Year-and-Fourth-Quarter-2025-Financial-Results))

Pipeline/regulatory milestones and commercial launches that change the medium-term growth mix. ([news.abbvie.com](https://news.abbvie.com/2026-02-04-AbbVie-Reports-Full-Year-and-Fourth-Quarter-2025-Financial-Results))

Changes in payer behavior or U.S. government pricing dynamics under ongoing policy implementation. ([news.abbvie.com](https://news.abbvie.com/2026-02-04-AbbVie-Reports-Full-Year-and-Fourth-Quarter-2025-Financial-Results))
company_overview: AbbVie is a global biopharmaceutical company that discovers, develops, manufactures, and sells therapies across multiple therapeutic areas. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1551152/000155115226000008/abbv-20251231.htm))

FY2025 net revenues were $61.160B, with major growth led by Immunology franchises (Skyrizi and Rinvoq) following Humira loss of exclusivity. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1551152/000155115226000008/abbv-20251231.htm))

FY2025 top franchise net revenues included Skyrizi ($17.562B), Rinvoq ($8.304B), and Humira ($4.540B). ([news.abbvie.com](https://news.abbvie.com/2026-02-04-AbbVie-Reports-Full-Year-and-Fourth-Quarter-2025-Financial-Results))
current_context: FY2025 delivered net revenues of $61.160B (+8.6% reported) and operating earnings of $15.075B. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1551152/000155115226000008/abbv-20251231.htm))

AbbVie guided FY2026 adjusted diluted EPS to $14.37 to $14.57 (excluding unfavorable acquired IPR&D and milestones expense impact). ([news.abbvie.com](https://news.abbvie.com/2026-02-04-AbbVie-Reports-Full-Year-and-Fourth-Quarter-2025-Financial-Results))

Management cited continued momentum for 2026 growth supported by innovation investments, and announced a multi-year U.S. investment commitment under a voluntary agreement (details in press release). ([news.abbvie.com](https://news.abbvie.com/2026-02-04-AbbVie-Reports-Full-Year-and-Fourth-Quarter-2025-Financial-Results))
investment_highlights: Base-case revenue growth assumes continued franchise resilience as Skyrizi and Rinvoq scale and Humira decline does not accelerate materially beyond current expectations. ([news.abbvie.com](https://news.abbvie.com/2026-02-04-AbbVie-Reports-Full-Year-and-Fourth-Quarter-2025-Financial-Results))

EBIT margin in the base case is modeled to normalize from 2024’s lower level toward a mid-20% range by maintaining operating leverage as revenue grows. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1551152/000155115226000008/abbv-20251231.htm))

D&A intensity and capex intensity are held near recent historical levels (D&A supported by the existing intangible asset base; capex from recent cash-flow trends). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1551152/000155115226000008/abbv-20251231.htm))

Working capital is modeled using the company’s structurally negative NWC profile (payables-heavy working capital), improving modestly toward less negative levels over time. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1551152/000155115226000008/abbv-20251231.htm))
key_risks: More severe-than-modeled pricing pressure (U.S. and international) and rebate/chargeback headwinds. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1551152/000155115226000008/abbv-20251231.htm))

Unexpected impairment charges or acquisition/IPR&D timing effects that distort GAAP operating earnings and tax outcomes. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1551152/000155115226000008/abbv-20251231.htm))
Greater working-capital cash drag if payables turnover, inventory, or accrual dynamics shift unfavorably.

presentation.subtitle: AbbVie (ABBV) — DCF base case with bull/bear sensitivities
valuation_summary: DCF base case chains explicit revenue growth and EBIT margin assumptions from FY2025, with a terminal growth rate of 2.0% and a terminal value built using an ‘average’ method between Gordon growth and an exit multiple.

The WACC (7.5%) and terminal multiple (14.0x) are set to reflect a large-cap, mature biopharma risk profile; bull/bear scenarios move discount rate, terminal growth, and operating assumptions modestly.
